result.title: Expanding the Decision Space of Pretrained Models through Structured Re-Decoding
result.summary: Native decoders limit how pretrained models combine local predictions under new structural constraints. We introduce Structured Re-Decoding (SRD), a training-free framework that constructs local candidates from model scores, samples, or external specifications, jointly optimizes their selection, and verifies reconstructed outputs. We show that candidate recombination expands feasible support and can improve attainable reward under a fixed KL divergence budget. Across molecular generation, protein design, RNA structure prediction, and antibody modeling, SRD enables improved structured inference, including verified molecules absent from the original sample pool. External chemical templates further extend SRD to noncanonical amino acids, peptide cyclization, and grammar-guided molecular construction. Preliminary experiments on a physical coherent Ising machine demonstrate the feasibility of hardware-based optimization, suggesting broader opportunities for quantum and quantum-inspired approaches to structured inference and combinatorial optimization across scientific domains.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练的结构化重解码框架（SRD）：从模型分数、采样或外部规范构造局部候选项，联合优化其选择并验证重建输出，应用于分子生成、蛋白设计、RNA 结构预测与抗体建模。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「候选生成—约束下联合选择—验证筛选」的推理期搜索流程，以及固定 KL 预算下扩展可行支撑的论证，可能为 LVR 的候选搜索、证据筛选与计算分配提供可供核查的方法线索，但任务域与视觉状态表示无直接联系。
